subject: Renewal amendment: capacity uplift + price safeguard
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@heliocloud.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Mar 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Renewal: HelioCloud - capacity + pricing proposal

Hi Asha,

Thanks again for running a great pilot with the inference cluster. As we look toward your 1-year renewal, here’s an option that preserves throughput while keeping unit economics attractive for HelioCloud: 

- Base commit: 1.2M token-units / month (12-month term)
- Incremental uplift (burst bucket): up to +30% capacity, billed at 25% discount vs list for any incremental usage above commit
- One-time credit: $40,000 applied to first invoice on execution (to offset recent overage during the onboarding month)
- Price hold: keep current unit rates fixed for the first 9 months of the renewal; thereafter rates revert to standard published list unless we agree to an extension

If this looks reasonable I suggest a quick 20–30 minute alignment call this week to lock the final numbers and timeline. Attached an initial term sheet for your review.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Initial_Renewal_Term_Sheet.pdf (pdf)]

From: Asha Rao <asha@heliocloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@heliocloud.com, James Tu <james.tu@heliocloud.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Mar 2027 18:03:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal: HelioCloud - capacity + pricing proposal

Marcus —

Thanks for the note and the term sheet. A few quick items from our side: 

1) The 9-month price hold is appreciated, but given our budget cycle we need a 12-month price hold on base rates.
2) The $40k credit helps but we also need an explicit true-up window for the onboarding overage (we want the ability to apply the credit against the March invoice vs it being held until Q2).
3) Can you confirm whether the burst capacity is guaranteed or subject to availability? For our production workload the burst needs priority routing.

Looping procurement and James (CFO). We can do a call Wed or Thu afternoon PT.

—Asha
Asha Rao
CTO, HelioCloud

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Mar 2027 09:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal: HelioCloud - capacity + pricing proposal

Asha, James —

Really appreciate the clarity. Quick responses to your asks: 

- Price hold: we can extend to 12 months on base rates if HelioCloud signs the renewal amendment by 31 Mar 2027.
- Credit application: we will allow the $40k credit to be applied to the March invoice (billing team will mark it as a one-time adjustment).
- Burst capacity: we can offer a "guaranteed burst" pool if HelioCloud commits to a modest uplift in the base commit: increase base to 1.4M token-units / month and we reserve a dedicated burst allocation with priority routing and a 20% surcharge on the burst ceiling (instead of the standard availability model).

Proposed counter (high level):
- Term: 12 months, start upon amendment signature
- Base commit: 1.4M token-units / month
- Incremental usage above commit: 25% discount on incremental unit price
- Guaranteed burst window: reserved capacity up to +30% with priority routing (applies when signed by 31 Mar)
- One-time credit: $40k applied to March invoice
- Price hold: 12 months on base unit rate if signed by 31 Mar

If that package is acceptable to HelioCloud I can ask legal to prepare a short amendment and Ben/Karthik can run the final commercials with your procurement team. I attached an updated counter for your review.

Thanks — happy to hop on Wed 3pm PT or Thu 11am PT.

Best,
Marcus
[Attachment: HelioCloud_Counter_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Mar 2027 11:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: HelioCloud – proposed concession math

Marcus / Ben —

Quick internal calc after reviewing the counter:

- Moving base from 1.2M to 1.4M increases committed revenue ~16.7% (mo basis).
- Offering a 12-month price hold reduces upside but improves renewal probability; modeled IRR stays positive given reduced risk of churn.
- $40k credit applied to March looks clean operationally; billing can post a one-time credit memo.
- Guaranteed burst reservation: we recommend structuring as a reserved pool with a small surcharge (proposed 20% on the reserved burst delta) to protect unit economics — margin impact is minor and gives procurement the SLA language they asked for.

Recommendation: accept the counter as-is (1.4M base, guaranteed +30% burst, 12-mo price hold if signed by 31 Mar) and push to legal for an amendment. Finance will want the concession P&L attached — I included the worksheet.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Sales Strategist | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Concession_P&L_calc.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@heliocloud.com>, James Tu <james.tu@heliocloud.com>, procurement@heliocloud.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 12:45:00 +0000
Subject: Final: Renewal amendment and next steps

Asha / James / procurement —

Thanks for the quick coordination. HelioCloud’s approval on the proposed package is great to hear. To confirm the agreed terms: 

- Term: 12 months (effective on amendment signature)
- Base commit: 1.4M token-units / month
- Incremental usage: 25% discount on any units above commit
- Guaranteed burst: reserved pool up to +30% with priority routing; 20% surcharge applied to the reserved delta
- Price hold: base unit rates fixed for 12 months if amendment is signed by 31 Mar 2027
- One-time credit: $40,000 applied to the March invoice (billing will post credit memo)

Next steps: 
1) I’ve asked Legal to prepare a short amendment (attached draft). Please review and share any redlines by Fri, Mar 12 so we can get this executed ahead of the sign-by date.
2) Finance: once amendment is executed we will provide the credit memo and updated invoice schedule.
3) Ops: we’ll schedule the reserved burst allocation and route it to HelioCloud’s region and priority pool on the contract effective date.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast turnaround. Looking forward to continuing to scale HelioCloud.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
